title: Implementing Light/Dark Mode Switcher
content: To implement the light/dark mode switcher, I used a toggle input with a checkbox type and styled it to look like a switch using CSS. I used JavaScript to create a change between light and dark mode with a change event. The change event adds a dark mode class to the body when activated. I also changed the text label in dark mode so it is labeled based on the mode that is activated, so it switches between "Light Mode" and "Dark Mode". I ran into some issues after adding this toggle switch on each page. For example, when switched to dark mode the toggle switch is barely visible due to the dark mode background color so I added a white outline. I also ran into a problem with the pages that contained containers that were white and made text disappear so I also made those containers change in dark mode.

title: Creating a Dynamic Blog Section
content: To create a dynamic blog section, I first started by making a JSON file called posts.json that contains all the blog post info such as title, date, and content. Then, I added the <div> element with the id called blog-list in the blog.html file which becomes a container for all the posts. The next step was making a JS file called scripts.js where I used JavaScript to fetch the JSON file and loop through. For each posts, I added a <div> element using the document.createElement and set its inner HTML with the title, date, content, and appended it to the blog-list container. I added a box container inside each post by styling them using CSS. At first when running the files, the posts werent appearing until I realized I forgot to link scripts.js file to the blog.html file and I linked them using the script tag.
